# `Q-22-9` — Unsupported Math Command

> A math command is recognized but has no rendering in the target format, or is a document-level command that has no meaning inside math.

## What this means

quarto-math knows the command (so this is not a typo) but cannot convert it: either the target format has no equivalent construct, or the command is not math at all (`\cite`, `\label`, `\includegraphics` inside `$…$`). The command is reported and the expression is emitted verbatim in formats that need a conversion.

## Why this happens

Common causes: document commands pasted into an equation, LaTeX-only typesetting commands such as `\raisebox`, or bra-ket notation from the `braket` package.

## How to fix it

Move document-level commands outside the math, or replace the construct with one the target supports. The diagnostic names the command and the reason.

## Where it is reported

Math diagnostics point into the `.qmd` at the exact characters inside the
`$…$` or `$$…$$` block, including math that spans several lines or sits
inside a block quote or list item. When a `\newcommand` macro is involved,
a problem inside the macro body points at the definition and a problem in
a macro argument points at the use.
